title: Use clear language
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plain English is mandatory; split sentences over 25 words; no more than 5 sentences per paragraph; active voice; short familiar words; specialists prefer plain English and specialist terms are explained on first use; 1 in 6 adults in England have very poor literacy skills; negative contractions are hard for many users

title: A to Z style guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Dates without ordinals or commas; "to" in ranges; times like 5:30pm, midday and midnight; numerals from 2; commas in numbers over 999; bullet point rules; sentence case and no block capitals; explain abbreviations on first use; "and" not ampersand; "select" not "click"; specific link text; avoid negative contractions; words to avoid

title: Publishing accessible documents
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Publish in HTML wherever possible; a new PDF is a last resort with an HTML version too; heading styles, simple tables with headers, alt text, no images of text, not relying on colour, meaningful link text, sans serif at least 12 point, left aligned, run the accessibility checker; updated 9 Oct 2025

title: Understanding accessibility requirements for public sector bodies
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Public sector websites and apps must meet WCAG 2.2 AA; schools and nurseries partly exempt but must make content needed to use a service accessible and publish an accessibility statement; charities exempt unless mostly publicly funded, providing essential services or aimed at disabled people; updated 30 Sep 2024

title: Plain language guide series
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Plain language is content the audience can understand; the Plain Writing Act of 2010 requires public content written for its audience; four guides on principles, writing, design and testing

title: Principles of plain language
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Write for your audience; plain language is not dumbing down; organise, keep it short and simple, avoid jargon; topic sentences, active voice, summaries up front, tables and lists

title: Writing for understanding
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Shorter words and sections, active voice and present tense; passive voice hides who acts; avoid hidden verbs (nouns made from verbs)

title: How to write clearly
publisher: Publications Office of the European Union (European Commission, Directorate-General for Translation)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Commission clear writing guide, released 16 Mar 2011, available in 23 EU languages (metadata page; guide text not read)

title: Get your document's readability and level statistics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. How to show Flesch Reading Ease and Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level in Word; Microsoft suggests about 60 to 70 for Reading Ease and about 7.0 to 8.0 for grade level in most documents; scores depend on sentence length and syllables; mixed-language caveats

title: How users read on the web
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Jakob Nielsen, article of 30 Sep 1997: 79% of test users scanned new pages and 16% read word by word; concise text measured 58% better usability, scannable layout 47%, objective language 27%, all three 124%

title: Voice and tone
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Voice stays the same while tone changes with the situation and the reader's feelings; voice traits plainspoken, genuine, translator, dry humour; clarity over entertainment; guide under a CC BY-NC 4.0 licence

title: An alt Decision Tree
supports: Opened with WebFetch. How to choose alt text: images of text, functional images in links or buttons, informative images with a short description, complex images with the information elsewhere on the page, decorative images with empty alt; updated 13 May 2024

title: Complex Images tutorial
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Charts and graphs need a short alt that identifies the image plus a long text description of the essential information, placed near the image or linked; updated 8 Apr 2026

title: Understanding SC 1.4.3: Contrast (Minimum)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Level AA contrast of at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (at least 18 point, or 14 point bold); logos and decorative text excepted; updated 4 Oct 2026

title: Understanding SC 2.4.4: Link Purpose (In Context)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Level A: the purpose of each link can be determined from its text or its surrounding context; context before the link works better for screen reader users; updated 4 Oct 2026

title: Improve accessibility with the Accessibility Checker
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Accessibility Checker in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and OneNote sorts issues into errors, warnings and tips; how to run it on Windows, Mac and the web, including while composing in Outlook

title: Email Accessibility Report 2026
supports: Opened with WebFetch. 376,348 emails analysed from May 2025 to May 2026 with Parcel's checker; 99.88% had serious or critical issues; 8 emails passed every check; common failures: missing lang and dir attributes, layout tables without role=presentation, links without discernible text, low colour contrast, images without alt text; .edu and .gov senders and major newsletter platforms all failed; last modified 21 May 2026

title: Email sender guidelines
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 1 Feb 2024 all senders to Gmail need SPF or DKIM, valid DNS, TLS and a spam rate below 0.3%; bulk senders (over 5,000 messages a day to Gmail) also need DMARC, alignment, one-click unsubscribe and a visible unsubscribe link; keep spam rate below 0.1%

title: Mail Privacy Protection
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Protect Mail Activity downloads remote content in the background whether or not the email is opened, and hides the IP address, so open signals are not reliable

title: Email marketing benchmarks and industry statistics
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Data as of December 2023: all users 35.63% open, 2.62% click, 0.22% unsubscribe; Education and Training 35.64% open, 3.02% click; Non-Profits 40.04% open, 3.27% click; notes that Apple privacy changes may affect open rates

title: CAN-SPAM Act: A Compliance Guide for Business
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Primary purpose test for commercial versus transactional or relationship email; accurate headers and subject lines; identify ads; valid postal address; opt-out honoured within 10 business days; penalties up to $53,088 per email; guide dated Aug 2023, edited Jan 2024

title: Data (Use and Access) Act factsheet: Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations
publisher: GOV.UK (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Section 114 extends the soft opt-in so charities can email and text people who have shown interest in their purposes, with an opt-out at collection and later; the Act comes into force in stages; published 27 Jun 2025

title: Data protection and online privacy
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Prior consent is required for direct marketing emails, with an exception for a company you already buy from marketing its own similar products; right to object at any time; cookie consent rules; last checked 5 Aug 2026

title: Fact sheet: new rule on the accessibility of web content and mobile apps
supports: Opened with WebFetch. ADA Title II rule covers state and local governments including public schools, colleges and universities; WCAG 2.1 AA; a 2026 interim final rule (20 Apr 2026) extended compliance to 26 Apr 2027 for populations of 50,000 or more and 26 Apr 2028 for smaller ones and special districts

title: A new era of inclusion begins: the European Accessibility Act enters into force
supports: Opened with WebFetch. From 28 June 2025 covered products and services must be accessible, including e-commerce, banking, e-books, transport websites and apps, and computers and phones

title: FAQs on photos and videos under FERPA
publisher: US Department of Education, Student Privacy Policy Office
supports: Opened with WebFetch. When a photo or video is an education record (directly related to a student and kept by the school); students in the background or at public events are usually not the focus; schools often designate public-event photos as directory information or get consent before sharing

title: Data protection in schools: taking and using photos and videos, and using CCTV
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Schools in England may rely on consent or legitimate interests for newsletters and marketing; start-of-year consent may not cover new uses; many schools collect specific consent for social media; privacy notices explain opt-out; a printed prospectus cannot be recalled after withdrawal but the photo must not be reused; personal photos by parents usually outside data protection law; updated 14 Oct 2026
